sections.h2: What do Indiana probate laws control when a homeowner dies?
sections.html:
Indiana probate laws sit in Title 29, Article 1 of the Indiana Code, and they decide who can act for the estate, who inherits, and how a house gets from the dead owner to a buyer. A relative living there or paying the bills has no power to sign a deed. Someone needs legal authority first.

That authority usually comes from a court appointment. Under IC 29-1-10-1, an executor named in a will comes first. If there is no will, the surviving spouse, or a person the spouse nominates, ranks ahead of the heirs, and the heirs come next. Minors and certain incapacitated people are disqualified no matter where they rank.

The same statute book also sets the deadlines that matter to a seller: the claims period, the window to contest a will, and the closing steps for the estate. Those clocks shape how quickly an inherited Indiana house can realistically change hands.

sections.h2: Who inherits an Indiana house when there is no will?
sections.html:
When no valid will exists, IC 29-1-2-1 sends the estate to relatives in a fixed order, and the house follows the same order as everything else. The spouse and the children are first in line, then parents, then siblings.

  • A surviving spouse with a child or a deceased child's descendants takes one half of the net estate. The rest goes to the descendants, shared equally when they are in the same generation.
  • A spouse with no descendants but a living parent takes three fourths. With no descendants and no parent, the spouse takes everything.
  • A second or later spouse who has no children with the decedent, where the decedent left children from an earlier marriage, takes 25 percent of the real property's net fair market value. That spouse still gets the usual share of personal property.
  • With no spouse and no descendants, the estate goes to surviving parents and to siblings and their descendants. Each parent counts as a sibling but receives at least one fourth.
  • If no relative in those groups survives, the statute works outward to grandparents, then to the decedent's aunts and uncles and their descendants, and finally to the state.

Co-heirs who inherit a house together each own a share. Any sale needs every owner to sign, so a missing or uncooperative heir can stall a closing for months.

sections.h2: Which probate numbers and deadlines should a seller know?
sections.html:
A handful of dollar limits and time windows drive most decisions about an inherited house in Indiana. The table collects the ones that come straight from the Indiana Code.

ItemRuleStatute
Small estate dollar limit$100,000 for deaths after June 30, 2022; $50,000 for deaths between mid-2006 and mid-2022; $25,000 before thatIC 29-1-8-1 and 29-1-8-3
Waiting period for the personal property affidavit45 days after death (5 days for vehicles and watercraft)IC 29-1-8-1
Spouse or minor children allowance$25,000; election due within 90 days after the order opening administrationIC 29-1-4-1
Creditor claimsBarred after 3 months from first published notice, with a 9 month outer limit from deathIC 29-1-14-1
Will contest3 months after the order admitting the willIC 29-1-7-17
Closing statement, unsupervised estateNo earlier than 3 months after first published notice to creditorsIC 29-1-7.5-4

The allowance deserves a second look. If the estate's personal property falls short of $25,000, the spouse or minor children can claim real estate for the difference, and the shortfall becomes a lien on the house. The real estate can be sold to satisfy it only with the consent of everyone interested or by court order after notice.

sections.h2: Can a small estate affidavit transfer an Indiana house?
sections.html:
The affidavit in IC 29-1-8-1 is built for personal property, so it does not by itself put a deed in a buyer's hands. It lets a distributee collect bank balances, securities, insurance benefits, safe deposit contents and similar assets, and it lets the Bureau of Motor Vehicles retitle a car, once 45 days have passed and no personal representative has been requested anywhere.

Real estate runs through IC 29-1-8-3. That section allows a fiduciary to distribute a qualifying estate without notice to creditors and then file a closing statement. If the estate includes land, an affidavit may be recorded with the county recorder where the property sits. It has to carry the legal description, a statement that the estate is within the dollar limit, the name and share of each person entitled to an interest, and an explanation of how each share was worked out.

Recording that affidavit is optional under the statute. Buyers and title companies still tend to want clear paper, so a seller should expect questions about who signed and on what authority.

sections.h2: How does an unsupervised estate sell or convey a house?
sections.html:
In an unsupervised estate, the personal representative can sell land without asking the judge each time. IC 29-1-7.5-3 lets the representative dispose of an asset, including land, for cash or on credit at public or private sale, and to sell, mortgage or lease estate real property.

The paperwork is spelled out. A deed from the representative is signed by the representative and can follow the statutory wording: it names the estate, the decedent, the cause number and the county, and it describes the real estate. IC 29-1-7.5-3.6 says a conveyance in that form is enough to pass all title to the grantee. IC 29-1-7.5-3.4 gives a similar form for handing real property to a devisee or heir.

When the estate closes, the representative's closing statement has to confirm that any real estate was conveyed by a recorded personal representative's deed. If nobody starts a proceeding within three months after the statement is filed, the appointment ends and the estate closes by operation of law.

sections.h2: What other paths skip probate for an Indiana house?
sections.html:
A recorded transfer on death deed is the main way an Indiana owner steers a house around probate. Under IC 32-17-14-11, the deed must be recorded with the county recorder before the owner dies, or it is void. It needs no consideration, no delivery and no auditor endorsement.

The type of ownership changes the effect:

  • Property held as tenants by the entirety stays out of reach unless the other spouse joins in the deed.
  • A joint tenancy with survivorship is severed and becomes a tenancy in common.
  • A life estate measured by the owner's life cannot be passed this way.

IC 32-21-1-15 adds a catch for later transfers. Once a transfer on death deed is on record, a later conveyance of the same property is void unless it was also recorded before the owner's death.

sections.h2: What do sellers of inherited Indiana houses usually run into?
sections.html:
Most delays come from authority, taxes and paperwork rather than from the market. Indiana property tax for a given year is billed the following year in two installments, due May 10 and November 10 under IC 6-1.1-22-9, so an estate can open with a tax bill already waiting. Counties also have to deal with weekend dates, and in 2026 the spring and fall dates were May 11 and November 10.

The deed itself passes through the county auditor and recorder. The auditor must endorse most deeds before the recorder accepts them, and a sales disclosure form is required with a transfer for value. DLGF materials list transfers from probate among those exempt from the form's fee.

  • Heirs live in different states and need to coordinate signatures.
  • No one has opened an estate, so nobody can sign for the owner.
  • The house needs work, and the estate has no cash for repairs or insurance.
  • Creditor claims remain open until the claims period runs.
  • A surviving spouse's allowance becomes a lien on the real estate.

Some families choose a cash sale to avoid carrying the repair and holding costs while the estate works through those steps. A buyer paying cash can often close once the personal representative or the heirs can deliver a deed, though a title company decides what paperwork it needs for each file.

sections.h2: Where do Indiana probate cases happen?
sections.html:
Indiana has 92 counties, and the estate is handled through the court system in the county where the case is opened. The five most populous counties in Wikipedia's county table are Marion, Lake, Allen, Hamilton and St. Joseph, and the smallest is Ohio County. Rules come from the statewide code, so the legal tests are the same, but forms, hearing schedules and clerk practices vary from one county to the next.

The recorder in the county where the land sits receives the personal representative's deed or any recorded affidavit, even if the owner lived elsewhere.

faqs.q: How long does probate take in Indiana?
faqs.a: There is no single timeline. The statutes set pieces of it: creditors have 3 months from the first published notice (with a 9 month cap from death), and an unsupervised representative can file a closing statement no earlier than 3 months after that notice. Contested wills, missing heirs and tax questions add time.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house in Indiana before probate is finished?
faqs.a: Yes, if the personal representative has authority. In an unsupervised estate the representative can sell land under IC 29-1-7.5-3 without a court order for each step. Without an appointment, no one has authority to sign for the estate.

faqs.q: What is the Indiana small estate limit in 2026?
faqs.a: The limit for deaths after June 30, 2022 is $100,000, measured on the gross probate estate after liens, encumbrances and reasonable funeral expenses. IC 29-1-8-3 adds administration costs and funeral expenses to the threshold for the real property procedure.

faqs.q: Does a small estate affidavit let me sell a house?
faqs.a: The affidavit in IC 29-1-8-1 is for collecting personal property. For land, IC 29-1-8-3 lets an affidavit be recorded with the county recorder, but the distribution runs through a fiduciary, and a buyer's title company may still ask for more.

faqs.q: How long can someone contest a will in Indiana?
faqs.a: An interested person has 3 months after the order admitting the will to probate. The contest must be in writing, verified by affidavit, and based on grounds such as lack of sound mind, improper execution, duress or fraud.

faqs.q: Does a recorded transfer on death deed avoid probate?
faqs.a: For that parcel, yes, if it was recorded with the county recorder before the owner died. An unrecorded deed is void, and a tenancy by the entirety needs the other spouse to join.
